links.outcome: Effect of AI-identity disclosure on intention to comply and return to same dentist
links.effect: Disclosure did not change intention to follow instructions but lowered likelihood of returning to same dentist (P<.01; Cohen d 0.35 and 0.37 for disclosed humanized and disclosed animated AI vs real person).
links.quote: Prior disclosure that the video was AI generated resulted in a lower willingness to return to the same dentist than the real-person condition ( P <.01; Cohen d =0.35 and 0.37 for the disclosed humanized AI and disclosed animated AI conditions, respectively).

links.outcome: Intention to comply when varying avatar gender across participant gender
links.effect: Women reported lower intention to comply with the female-presenting avatar (mean 6.37) than the male one (mean 6.69; P=.05; d=-0.35); men showed no sizable difference (P=.30). Interaction P=.04.
links.quote: However, women reported a significantly lower intention to comply when the video featured a female-presenting humanized avatar (mean 6.37, SD 1.24) than when it featured the man version (mean 6.69, SD 0.50; 95% CI −0.66 to 0.00; P =.05; Cohen d =−0.35).

links.outcome: intention to follow instructions versus real person
links.effect: Animated AI: mean 6.27 vs real person 6.52; 95% CI −0.48 to −0.04; P=.02; Cohen d=0.28.
links.quote: However, those who viewed the animated AI avatar were significantly less likely to follow the instructions (mean 6.27, SD 1.05, 95% CI −0.48 to −0.04; P =.02; Cohen d =0.28).

links.outcome: AI disclosure effects on trust and compliance

links.effect: Experiment 1: no comprehension differences; P=.92 for perfect scores and P≥.07 for average score.
links.quote: However, there were no significant differences in comprehension across any of the video conditions ( P =.92 for the percentage achieving perfect scores and P ≥.07 for the average score).
